Park Ji‑sung (박지성) is a retired South Korean professional footballer born on August 25, 1981, in Seoul, South Korea. He played primarily as a midfielder and is best known for his long and successful career at the English Premier League club Manchester United.

**Key highlights of his career:**

| Period | Club | Notable achievements |
|--------|------|----------------------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | Won the K League title and the Asian Club Championship |
| 2000–2005 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | Won the Dutch league twice (2004, 2005) and the KNVB Cup (2004) |
| 2005–2012 | Manchester United (Premier League) | Won the Premier League (2007, 2008), FA Cup (2009), UEFA Champions League (2008), and FIFA Club World Cup (2008). He was also named the club’s “Player of the Year” in 2008. |
| 2012–2013 | FC Tokyo (J1 League) | Helped the club win the J.League Cup (2013) |
| 2013–2014 | Ulsan Hyundai (K League) | Won the Korean FA Cup (2014) |

**International career:**

- Represented South Korea at the 2002 FIFA World Cup, where the team reached the semi‑finals, and at the 2006 FIFA World Cup.
- Earned 108 caps for the national team, scoring 12 goals.
- Served as captain of the national team from 2008 until his retirement from international football in 2014.

**Playing style and reputation:**

- Known for his stamina, work rate, and versatility, capable of playing both defensive and attacking midfield roles.
- Nicknamed “The Iron Man” for his durability and consistency.
- Widely regarded as one of the greatest Asian footballers of all time.

**Post‑retirement:**

- After retiring from professional play, Park Ji‑sung has been involved in various football-related activities, including coaching, punditry, and ambassadorial roles for football development in South Korea. He has also worked as a football analyst for Korean sports networks and has participated in charity and community outreach programs.
